---
applyTo: "packages/react/runtime/**"
---

When updating runtime snapshot tests for preview preact builds that carry named children props like `$0` and slot-index semantics, keep `list` host snapshots isolated from surrounding `view`/`text` snapshots by creating a standalone `__SNAPSHOT__(<list>{HOLE}</list>)` and inserting it into the outer snapshot.
Do not drop `packages/react/runtime/__test__/list.test.jsx` cases added on `main`; preserve nested-list recording and `__DestroyLifetime` callback cleanup assertions while adapting expectations to the new snapshot structure.
For ReactLynx `Children`, reuse `preact/compat` behavior and derive types from `typeof PreactChildren`; only override `map`, `forEach`, and `toArray` to expose readonly frozen arrays.
When adding snapshot runtime tests that manually construct `SnapshotInstance` or `BackgroundSnapshotInstance`, remember that the managers' `clear()` methods intentionally do not reset `nextId`; use explicit ids or restore `nextId` in the test to avoid unrelated inline snapshot churn.
Keep devtools Lepus helpers that only need snapshot instance lookup importing the minimal `snapshotInstanceManager` module instead of the full snapshot implementation, so the main-thread transform can retain the singleton without pulling unrelated snapshot runtime code.
When adding React runtime ALOG diagnostics, guard the entire formatting path with `typeof __ALOG__ !== 'undefined' && __ALOG__`, call `console.alog?.(...)`, and keep `JSON.stringify` inside the guard so disabled logging does not add serialization work.
Keep builtin attribute-name conversion for JSX spreads aligned across Snapshot and Element Template. Centralize attribute and event-key recognition in `src/shared/attribute-name.ts`; keep `transformAttrName` responsible only for name conversion and use `isEventPropKey` explicitly on the transformed name where event classification is required. When a React-style event key is renamed, emit the transformed native event key but preserve the original spread key in the event value so the background runtime can recover the handler. Keep `updateSpread` ordering stable; convert marked spread keys while collecting list-item platform info instead of moving the full spread transform ahead of list processing. Keep `extractListItemPlatformInfo` a pure filter for normalized attribute names: only values carrying the raw `__spread` marker should have their keys transformed, because known spread values without the marker may already be normalized and custom rename rules are not necessarily idempotent.
Read runtime build configuration from the page-scoped `lynx.__runtime_configs__`.
For third-party stateful APIs that have different dual-thread semantics, expose the adapter from a dedicated `@lynx-js/*` companion package and map that package's public request by issuer layer in `plugin-react-alias`; do not add the third-party packages to `@lynx-js/react` dependencies. Keep main-thread implementations read-only for first-screen rendering: setters may report a development error but must not mutate, and effects or subscriptions must not execute callbacks. Preact Signals consumers import `@lynx-js/react-signals`; that package owns the Preact Signals dependencies and matching `lepus` implementation.
For typed `MainThreadValue` handles, create the real main-thread object through a registered factory and track hydrated objects in a `WeakSet`. Do not attach React bookkeeping fields to third-party objects, and preserve the existing `MainThreadRef` wire shape when no custom type is present.
